conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. You're in the hospital now. Can you tell me your name?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah… it's James. What’s going on? I was just on the couch.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You were found unresponsive earlier. We know you’ve been drinking and may have taken something else. Your oxygen was low and you have pneumonia. We’re keeping you for treatment.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Pneumonia again? I just got told I had that yesterday. I need my meds though. I’m on methadone.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked with your doctor. He hasn’t prescribed methadone in a month because your urine tests have been negative. We can’t give it now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What? That’s bullshit! I need it. I’m in pain. I’m leaving then.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand you’re upset, but you’re very sick. Your oxygen dropped this morning, and you’re not well enough to leave.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t care. I’m getting out of here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You pulled out your IV. Security is here to help keep you safe. We’re not restraining you, but we need to make sure you don’t hurt yourself.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m not staying if you won’t help my pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re helping your pain with other safe options. But methadone isn’t safe for you right now. Let’s focus on your pneumonia and breathing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Fine. But I’m not doing any more tests.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning, James. Your oxygen was low again this morning—87%—so we put you on more oxygen. It’s better now at 95% on nasal cannula.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I felt short of breath. Is it the pneumonia?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Partly. Your chest X-ray shows improvement in the infection, but we’re concerned it’s not the only issue. The team wanted to do a CT scan to check for a blood clot, but you refused.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t want more scans. I’ve had enough. Is the antibiotic working?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You got levofloxacin in the ER, but last time you were here, the infection was resistant to it. So we’ve switched you to Bactrim, which should work better based on your sputum culture.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I’m on new antibiotics now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, twice a day. We also think your COPD might be flaring. We offered breathing treatments, but you declined.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I hate those nebs. They make me shaky.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. But they help open your airways. Maybe we can try a lower dose?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Not right now. Maybe later.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: James, your labs show high sodium and high bicarbonate. That’s from dehydration and possibly from drinking a lot and not eating. Your liver enzymes are also a bit high, which is common with alcohol use.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Am I in liver failure?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, not at all. But it’s a sign your body is under stress from alcohol. We’re giving you fluids and monitoring you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know I drink. But I can’t stop here. I need to get back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re going through alcohol withdrawal. That’s why we’re giving you diazepam every few hours. You’ve had 60 mg in the last 24 hours. Stopping suddenly could cause seizures.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve done it before. I’ll be fine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: This time is different. You’re weaker, and your body is fighting infection. Leaving now is risky.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also offered nicotine patches since you smoke, but you declined.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t need help quitting. I’ve got bigger problems.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also asked if you’d speak with a social worker about housing and support. You said no.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What’s the point? Nobody helps anyway.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: James, you’ve been here two days. Your pneumonia is improving, but you’ve only had two doses of the right antibiotic. You really should stay for at least five days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m leaving. I can’t stay here anymore. I feel better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I have to tell you, leaving AMA—against medical advice—means you’re at high risk of getting worse, maybe even dying.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know. But I’m going. I’ll take the pills with me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We can give you a prescription for Bactrim. But please, if you start feeling worse—short of breath, fever, confusion—come back right away.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I’ll think about it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’ll have the nurse give you discharge papers. Please take care of yourself, James.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks… for trying.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We care about your health. If you change your mind, we’re here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll be okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take this prescription and the contact for the clinic. Please follow up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re officially leaving against medical advice. We’ve documented that you understand the risks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I understand.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care, James.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah. Bye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse will assist you with discharge.
